rounds.answer:
The exact current marker is INTERVIEW-66-2036b742ae76e85a.

Use dynamic programming with two running totals: the best sum for the previous prefix and for the prefix before that. For each value, choose the larger of skipping it or taking it plus the best sum from two positions back, then advance both totals.

The invariant is that these totals remain the optimal sums for their respective prefixes, with no adjacent houses selected. Initialize both to zero: an empty array returns zero, a single house returns its value, and all-zero input returns zero. This takes O(n) time and O(1) extra space; solve(nums) returns the result without stdin/stdout, imports, or exports.

Use subset-sum dynamic programming: if the total is odd, return false; otherwise, check whether a subset sums to half the total. Its complement then has the same sum.

Invariant: after processing each prefix, reachable[s] is true exactly when some subset of that prefix sums to s. Initially only zero is reachable; update sums downward for each value so that value cannot be reused.

Boundary cases: empty input and all zeros return true; a single positive value returns false; duplicates are separate usable elements; an even total can still be impossible, as with [2, 2, 2].

Time is O(n × target), with O(target + 1) space, where target is half the total. No implementation yet.

Maintain a tails array, where tails[k] is the smallest possible ending value of any strictly increasing subsequence of length k + 1 among the elements processed. For each number, binary-search for the first tail greater than or equal to it and replace that tail; if none exists, append the number.

This preserves the invariant: a smaller ending value leaves at least as much room for future extensions. The tails array stays strictly increasing, and its length is the answer, although its entries need not themselves form a subsequence.

Boundary cases: empty input returns 0; one element returns 1; all equal or decreasing values return 1; strictly increasing input returns its full length. Equal values replace rather than extend, and negative integers need no special handling.

Time: O(n log n). Auxiliary space: O(n).

Use dynamic programming, scanning rows from left to right with one rolling array. Initialize the starting cell to its value; every other cell gets its value plus the smaller available cost from above or left. Return the bottom-right cost, counting both endpoints.

Invariant: before updating a cell, dp[col] holds the minimum cost from above, and dp[col - 1], when present, holds the updated minimum cost from the left. Every path enters from one of those two neighbors, so choosing the smaller preserves optimality.

Boundary cases: a single cell returns its value; the first row and first column use cumulative sums because only one predecessor exists. Single-row or single-column grids have exactly one path, and zeros work normally. Empty grids are outside the stated nonempty contract.

Time: O(rows × columns); auxiliary space: O(columns).
